project.name: Urban Eye 3D
project.description: JOSM plugin for 3D visualization of buildings

tags.description: This tag causes a feature that would otherwise be considered linear to be considered polygonal.
The feature is interpreted as barrier, in case it does not have the building tag.
The main tag for identifying a building outline.
Specifies the color of the building's walls.
An alternative tag for the total height of the building, including the roof, in meters.

Specifies the orientation of the roof ridge, typically 'along' or 'across' the longer axis of the building.
Roof is oriented across the longest side of the building.
Roof is oriented along the longest side of the building. This is default value
A gabled roof with a semicircular apse at one end. The apex of the apse is located above the middle of the longest side of the base.
A synonym for pyramidal. Rises to a single point. To generate a smooth cone, the building outline should be a circle with a sufficient number of nodes.
Two gabled roof sections at right angles. Only supported for quadrangular footprints. `roof:orientation` and `roof:direction` have no effect.
A synonym for cross_gabled. Two gabled roof sections put together at right angles. Only quadrangular footprints are supported.
A hemispherical roof suitable for any base shape. A circular base produces a traditional dome, while a rectangular base produces a modern, elongated dome.
A standard flat roof. A fascia (vertical decorative band) is created if `roof:height` or `roof:levels` are specified.
Classic pitched roof. Orientation can be controlled with `roof:orientation=along|across`. `roof:direction` is also supported but snaps to the nearest axis.
A symmetrical two-sided roof with two slopes on each side. The orientation can be specified with the `roof:orientation` tag.
Half of a dome, with the apex located above the middle of the longest side of the base. Useful for orthodox church apses.
A mix of gabled and hipped styles. Orientation can be set with `roof:orientation`. Only supported for quadrangular building outlines.
All sides slope down to the walls. Generated using a straight skeleton algorithm, which can create complex shapes for non-convex buildings.
A four-sided gambrel-style hip roof with two slopes on each side. Currently only supported for quadrangular building outlines.
Interpreted as hipped for buildings (as better than flat), but not for building parts
An onion-shaped dome. The building outline defines the tholobate (drum), and the onion dome is generated on top of it, getting wider than the base.
A roof that rises to a single point, generated from an arbitrary base outline. `roof:orientation` and `roof:direction` have no effect.
A semi-cylindrical or hangar-like roof. Its orientation can be controlled with the `roof:orientation` tag.
Generates a roof with an off-center flat top. This implementation follows the F4 map interpretation, which may differ from a classic single-ridge saltbox roof.
A roof half-hipped from one side and gabled from the other. Orientation is controlled by `roof:direction`. Supported for quadrangular footprints only.
A roof hipped from one side and gabled from the other. Orientation is controlled by `roof:direction`. Supported for quadrangular footprints only.
A single-sloped roof surface (a lean-to). The slope direction is controlled by the `roof:direction` tag, which can be set to any angle.
Building or man-made object has hyperboloid shape. Useful for cooling towers and chimneys. Homebrew SM3DB extension
Indicates that the pitch is used for soccer. Triggers rendering of soccer markings.
Indicates that the pitch is used for tennis. Triggers rendering of tennis court markings.
Defines the height of each individual step for building:part=steps. 0.16 is used as default
Members of building relation can be downloaded automatically, to prevent incomplete buildings
Members of a multipolygon relation can be downloaded automatically to prevent broken geometry
Alternative for building:part=roof. In case of building:part=yes + wall=no walls are not generated and roof floats
Used to override building:part=roof. For building:part=roof + wall=yes walls are still created
Width of the feature. Primarily used for barriers
